New machine. Its objects are: gilisak, binirel, kebivu, nopumen, natumes, ladetes.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects together to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: gilisak, binirel, kebivu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three didn't light it up. Next I'll test two of the other three objects together to see how the machine reacts.

TEST: nopumen, natumes
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither group lit up. If any single nexiom were enough to light the machine, there could be at most one nexiom (ladetes), which is impossible. So the machine probably needs both nexioms together, or follows some other rule. I'll test all six objects at once to check whether having both nexioms present makes it light.

TEST: gilisak, binirel, kebivu, nopumen, natumes, ladetes
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither group of three lit up, but all six together did. So the machine most likely lights only when both nexioms are on it. That leaves 11 possible pairs. This test splits them into 5 that would light it and 6 that would not.

TEST: gilisak, binirel, ladetes, nopumen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither group of three lit the machine, but all six together did. So it most likely lights only when both nexioms are on it. The last test lit up, so both nexioms are among gilisak, binirel, ladetes and nopumen. Gilisak with binirel is ruled out by the first test. That leaves 5 possible pairs: gilisak–ladetes, gilisak–nopumen, binirel–ladetes, binirel–nopumen and ladetes–nopumen.

Two yes/no tests can only separate 4 cases, so I can't guarantee a certain answer. I'll split the 5 pairs as evenly as I can. This test lights for 3 of them (gilisak–ladetes, gilisak–nopumen, ladetes–nopumen) and stays dark for the other 2 (binirel–ladetes, binirel–nopumen).

TEST: gilisak, nopumen, ladetes
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine seems to light only when both nexioms are on it: neither group of three lit it, but all six together did. On that basis, the last test not lighting rules out gilisak–ladetes, gilisak–nopumen and ladetes–nopumen. The two pairs left are binirel–ladetes and binirel–nopumen. Both include binirel, so the open question is whether the second nexiom is ladetes or nopumen.

I'll test binirel and ladetes on their own. If the machine lights, the nexioms are binirel and ladetes. If it doesn't, they are binirel and nopumen. This answer still rests on the "both needed" rule, which fits every result so far but which I haven't confirmed directly.

TEST: binirel, ladetes
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Assuming the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, the last test not lighting rules out binirel–ladetes. That leaves **binirel and nopumen**, and this pair fits all six results:
- Test 1 (gilisak, binirel, kebivu): only binirel was present, so no light.
- Test 2 (nopumen, natumes): only nopumen was present, so no light.
- Test 3 (all six objects): both were present, so it lit.
- Test 4 (gilisak, binirel, ladetes, nopumen): both were present, so it lit.
- Test 5 (gilisak, nopumen, ladetes): only nopumen was present, so no light.
- Test 6 (binirel, ladetes): only binirel was present, so no light.

The answer depends on that "both needed" rule. It fits every result, but I never tested it directly. A different rule could in principle fit the same results and point to another pair.

ANSWER: nexioms = binirel, nopumen
One last question. If only binirel were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. Test 1 had binirel on the machine with gilisak and kebivu, and it stayed dark. If binirel and nopumen are the nexioms, gilisak and kebivu are not, and non-nexioms never affect the machine. So test 1 behaved exactly as binirel alone would.

This depends on my answer being correct. If gilisak or kebivu were actually a nexiom, test 1 would not settle it. But binirel alone staying dark also fits the "both needed" rule, which explains all six results.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: simuzul, litofen, vilator, rikoris, zovedos, fezogik.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing a single object to see how the machine responds to it.

TEST: simuzul
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

simuzul alone didn't light it, so next I'll test three of the other objects together.

TEST: litofen, vilator, rikoris
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither simuzul nor the trio litofen, vilator, rikoris lit the machine. Next I'll test the two untested objects together. If the machine lights whenever any nexiom is present, these two must be the nexioms. If it needs both nexioms at once, this tells me whether they are this exact pair.

TEST: zovedos, fezogik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Nothing has lit up yet, so the machine does not light whenever any nexiom is present. If it did, zovedos and fezogik would have had to be the nexioms, and that pair failed. It might need both nexioms together, or something else, like exactly one nexiom. Next I'll test a mixed group of one object from each earlier test.

TEST: simuzul, litofen, zovedos
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

simuzul, litofen and zovedos lit the machine together, but every earlier group did not. Two rules fit these results:

- **The machine lights only when both nexioms are on it.** The pair must then be simuzul+litofen, simuzul+zovedos or litofen+zovedos.
- **The machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is on it.** The pair must then be zovedos+fezogik, litofen+vilator or litofen+rikoris.

Testing simuzul and litofen splits these six cases in half:
- If it lights, the answer is simuzul+litofen, litofen+vilator or litofen+rikoris.
- If it does not, the answer is simuzul+zovedos, litofen+zovedos or zovedos+fezogik.

With only one test left after this, I can't narrow six cases down to one for certain, so I may have to guess at the end.

TEST: simuzul, litofen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The last test lit the machine, which leaves three possibilities:
- **Both nexioms needed:** the pair is simuzul + litofen.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** the pair is litofen + vilator.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** the pair is litofen + rikoris.

A single lit-or-not test can split three cases only into a single case and a pair, so I can't be certain of the answer. Testing vilator alone does that split:
- If it lights, the answer must be litofen + vilator.
- If it does not, the answer is either simuzul + litofen or litofen + rikoris, and I'll have to pick one of those two.

TEST: vilator
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Two answers still fit every result, so this is a guess between them:
- **Simuzul + litofen**, if the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it.
- **Litofen + rikoris**, if the machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is on it.

Vilator alone not lighting ruled out litofen + vilator, but it could not separate these last two. I'm choosing simuzul + litofen because "lights only when both are present" seems the more likely rule for a detector. Litofen is a nexiom in both cases.

ANSWER: nexioms = simuzul, litofen
One last question. If only litofen were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

I don't know for sure, because the two explanations I couldn't separate disagree here:
- **Both nexioms needed (simuzul + litofen):** litofen alone is only one nexiom, so the machine would not light.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed (litofen + rikoris):** litofen alone is exactly one nexiom, so the machine would light.

In my answer I went with the "both nexioms needed" rule. Under that rule, litofen alone would not light it up. That conclusion is only as reliable as my earlier guess between the two rules.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: lekilis, fitagak, givemak, sibebor, barini, sinise.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half of the objects on the machine to see whether any nexioms are among them.

TEST: lekilis, fitagak, givemak
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up, so it holds at least one nexiom. Next I'll test the other three objects to see whether they also contain one.

TEST: sibebor, barini, sinise
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up and the second did not. Under most simple rules, that puts both nexioms among lekilis, fitagak and givemak. I'll test lekilis on its own to start narrowing these down.

TEST: lekilis
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Both nexioms seem to be among lekilis, fitagak and givemak, but I still don't know the machine's rule.
- If it lights when any nexiom is present, lekilis staying dark means the pair is fitagak and givemak.
- If it only lights when both nexioms are present, lekilis alone being dark tells me nothing, and lekilis could still be one of the pair.

Testing fitagak and givemak together checks both cases. If it lights, the pair is fitagak and givemak under either rule. If it stays dark, lekilis must be one of the nexioms.

TEST: fitagak, givemak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Only an "AND" rule fits all four results, where the machine lights up only when both nexioms are on it.
- **"Any nexiom" rule ruled out:** if one nexiom were enough, lekilis alone and fitagak + givemak would both have stayed dark. That leaves no nexiom in the first group, yet it lit up.
- **"Exactly one nexiom" rule ruled out:** lekilis alone stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom. Then only one of fitagak or givemak can be a nexiom, since the pair stayed dark. That puts the second nexiom in the last three objects, and that group should have lit up, but it didn't.
- **"AND" rule fits:** the first group must contain both nexioms. Fitagak + givemak stayed dark, so lekilis is one of them. The other is fitagak or givemak.

Testing lekilis with fitagak settles it. If it lights up, the pair is lekilis and fitagak. If it stays dark, the pair is lekilis and givemak.

TEST: lekilis, fitagak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Only the "AND" rule fits so far, where the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it.
- Under that rule, lekilis must be one nexiom and the other must be fitagak or givemak.
- Lekilis with fitagak stayed dark, so the pair should be **lekilis and givemak**.

I'll use my last test to check this. If lekilis with givemak lights up, it confirms both the pair and the rule.

TEST: lekilis, givemak
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Lekilis with givemak lit up, which confirms that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it. All six results fit that rule:
- **Lit up:** lekilis + fitagak + givemak, and lekilis + givemak. Both sets contain lekilis and givemak.
- **Stayed dark:** sibebor + barini + sinise, lekilis alone, fitagak + givemak, and lekilis + fitagak. Each of these is missing at least one of the pair.

ANSWER: nexioms = lekilis, givemak
One last question. If only givemak were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. Everything I saw fits one rule: the machine lights only when both nexioms, lekilis and givemak, are on it together.

- **Lit up:** both lit sets contained lekilis and givemak.
- **Stayed dark:** every dark set had at most one nexiom. Lekilis alone stayed dark, and so did fitagak + givemak, where givemak was the only nexiom present.

I never tested givemak by itself, so this is a prediction. Givemak alone would have only one nexiom, so it should stay dark, just as lekilis did on its own.

PROBE: no
